name: Just-in-time production at Toyota
summary: From 1948 Toyota had each process fetch only the parts it needed from the one before, signalled by kanban cards from 1953, which cut stocks and was later copied abroad.
description: Under Taiichi Ohno, Toyota adopted a pull system of production in 1948, in which the later process goes back to the earlier one to take only the parts it needs. Ohno says the kanban card, an idea he took from American supermarkets, was applied in the machine shop at the main plant in 1953. Kanban became company-wide in 1962 by Ohno's account and in 1963 by Toyota's own history, which also records some suppliers joining from 1963.

impact.note: It reorganised production around low stocks and pull (depth 2) and lean manufacturing and its offshoots grew from it (generativity 2), but Britannica credits it with changing methods 'in some industries', one sector across many countries, so reach is lowered from the lead's 2 to 1.

why: Ohno hoped that the supermarket method would help Toyota approach its just-in-time goal.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Company-wide kanban: Ohno's book says 1962, Toyota's history says 1963. Both are recorded; which is right is unsettled.
Toyota's history lists a 1954 fill-up system at machining plants; how it relates to the 1953 kanban use needs checking.
The copy of Ohno's book used here is a third-party upload of a book in copyright; a publisher or library copy should replace it as the cited URL.
Ford's flow production, which Ohno also discusses as a forerunner, was not examined as a rival to the first-known claim.

research.note: Encyclopaedia Britannica describes just-in-time manufacturing as a system 'developed by Toyota Motor Corp. and imported to the West', and Ohno calls its concepts 'totally new'; his supermarket model was a retail restocking practice, not an earlier production system, so it is recorded under prompted_by and not as a derivation.
